thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: high tail latency observed for streaming responses in eu-west-1. p95 token latency > 1200ms for last 10m, concurrent connections spiking. auto-mitigation not triggered. paging oncall.

maya (oncall): I'm on it. can someone grab which service is hottest? logs show repeated sse connection churn and OOM retries on runtime-gpu-3.

kevin (runtime): Runtime reports per-connection kv-cache pressure. streaming paths keep large active KV states across many small sessions. looks like a workload mismatch (lots of short chats with streaming enabled).

tina (sre): I can start shaping traffic at the LB level but first quick option: disable streaming responses regionally to reduce long-lived connections. that should free sockets and reduce per-host memory.

alex (product): What's the expected user-visible impact? want to pre-signal support and major customers.

kevin (runtime): Customers will fall back to chunked polling / non-streamed single-response behavior. TTF-first-token might be slightly higher (~100-200ms) but stable. No token loss.

jorge (support): I'll draft a short message for top 5 enterprise customers affected in eu-west-1 and keep support channel on standby.

maya (oncall): Plan: 1) coordinate region flag flip to disable streaming in eu-west-1, 2) apply temporary ingress rate limiting to protect control-plane, 3) monitor p95/p99 for 15m, 4) revert when stable. Need approvals from runtime and ops. :thumbsup:

kevin (runtime): Approved. I'll prepare the toggle and a canary on runtime-gpu-4 first. nora, can you watch telemetry?

nora (eng): watching traces and memtables. setting up dashboards: streaming_conn_count, kv_cache_size, p95_stream_latency, overall_cpu.

kevin (runtime): Command to flip feature toggle (internal ops service):

```
curl -u deploy-bot:REDACTED -X POST https://ops.internal/api/feature-toggle \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"feature":"streaming_responses","enabled":false,"region":"eu-west-1","reason":"incident-2801112222"}'
```

kevin (runtime): Alternatively, for runtime configmap patch (k8s):

```
kubectl -n runtime patch configmap runtime-features -p '{"data":{"streaming_responses.eu-west-1":"false"}}'
```
deploy-bot: deploy request received for feature-toggle change by kevin. CI checks passed. scheduled to run.

maya (oncall): I'm executing the curl now. posting here before run.

maya (oncall): RUN: executed toggle at 2801112250.

deploy-bot: feature-toggle updated: streaming_responses disabled in eu-west-1. change-id: ft-20280311-04.

nora (eng): Telemetry: streaming_conn_count dropping ~70% in 60s. kv_cache_size on runtime hosts decreasing. p95_stream_latency trending down. CPU load reduced on runtime-gpu-3.

tina (sre): LB shaping: added connection cap per-node 1200 -> 800 as buffer. applied and held. No sign of queueing at LB.

maya (oncall): Monitoring p95/p99 for next 15m. if stable for 15 we consider it mitigated.

jorge (support): Draft message sent to oncall-support channel and queued to top customers. Template: "We're temporarily disabling streaming responses in eu-west-1 to improve stability and reduce latency; you may see slightly longer single-response latencies. We're monitoring and will update in 15 minutes."

alex (product): Good. add a note that webhooks and callback integrations are unaffected.

nora (eng): p95 latency (all inference) dropped from 1.6s -> 480ms over 5m. p99 still elevated but falling.

maya (oncall): After 15m checks: p95 stable ~450-500ms, p99 trending towards previous baseline. marking as MITIGATED for streaming-related spike. moving to verification.

kevin (runtime): Next steps before re-enable: 1) increase per-connection memory cap, 2) add short-lived session eviction for idle streaming sessions, 3) implement polite 503 backpressure for new streaming connections at 95% mem. We'll stagger re-enable after those are live.

tina (sre): Ops note: document the rollback commands. Also filed a ticket to escalate autoscaling policies for runtime pools.

maya (oncall): Re-enable window plan: don't flip back globally until mem cap changes are live and canaries pass. tentative ETA 4 hours. I'll hand off to oncall-sre for overnight.

sam (ops): I will coordinate the capacity bump and schedule canary re-enable on runtime-gpu-6 in 3 hours, watch for connection churn.

kevin (runtime): Putting the re-enable checklist here:
- run canary (runtime-gpu-6) with streaming enabled for 10m
- observe p95/p99 and kv_cache memory usage
- if stable, stagger region-wide enable with 5-minute pauses and runbook checks

maya (oncall): Thanks everyone. tagging incident as "streaming_quiet_mode_eu-west-1". created follow-up ticket INF-4821 for root-cause and long-term fixes.

jorge (support): I'll update customers with final note once re-enable happens.

incident-bot: Incident update: MITIGATED (streaming connections limited) — incident closed to active response; follow-ups filed.

maya (oncall): closing thread. will re-open if regressions. :white_check_mark:
